mainTopic: Which crevices and rocks are measured with a field, both for הקדש and for a sale
overview: The amud opens at the end of a משנה in ערכין about someone who is מקדיש a field. Crevices or rocks of ten טפחים are not measured with the field, while smaller ones are. The גמרא asks why the big ones are not at least consecrated as separate plots. A ברייתא shows that even tiny fields can be consecrated, so their small size is not the reason. רב עוקבא בר חמא answers that those crevices are full of water and cannot be planted, and the small ones are just ordinary 'cracks' and 'spines' of the field. For a sale, רב פפא says deep crevices are left out even when dry, because a buyer does not want a field that looks split into pieces. Then the amud limits how much small rocky ground counts with a sold field: up to four קבין, spread over five קבין or, per רבי יוחנן, over most of the field. A question about an uneven spread ends in תיקו, and רבי ירמיה begins a new question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Deep crevices and tall rocks are not measured with the field
steps.stepSummary: The ending of a משנה in ערכין about הקדש: crevices or rocks of ten טפחים or more are not measured with the field, and smaller ones are.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are not measured together with it. Less than this, they are measured together with it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a משנה in ערכין, quoted by the גמרא, about a person who is מקדיש his field. It gives the rule for crevices and rocks: ten טפחים or more are not measured with the field, and less than ten are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A crevice ten טפחים deep, or a rock ten טפחים tall, is treated as a separate area, so it is left out of the field's measurement. Anything smaller is simply part of the field. This rule is the starting point for the question that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: are measured together with it (the field)
less than this amount (less than ten טפחים)

phrases.english: they are not measured together with it.
phrases.notes: "They" are crevices deeper, or rocks taller, than ten טפחים, and "it" is the consecrated field.

phrases.english: Less than this, they are measured together with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה in ערכין that the גמרא began quoting just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a consecrated field, crevices or rocks of ten טפחים are left out of the field's measurement, while smaller ones are included.

steps.title: Why aren't the crevices consecrated on their own?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the deep crevices and tall rocks are not part of the field, why aren't they at least consecrated as their own pieces?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let them be consecrated by themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה in ערכין. If these areas are not counted with the field, they should at least become הקדש separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the crevices out of the field's measurement does not mean the owner did not consecrate them. So the גמרא argues they should count as their own consecrated plots, with their own redemption. The משנה, though, seems to treat them as not counting at all.

phrases.english: But why?
Let them be consecrated by themselves!

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the משנה in ערכין that crevices of ten טפחים are not measured with the field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being excluded from the field's measurement should not cancel their consecration. They should count as separate consecrated areas.

steps.title: A suggested answer: too small to be consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a possible answer: since each crevice is smaller than a בית כור, it cannot be consecrated on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: since it is not a בית כור, they are not consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer to its own question, but it is only a suggestion. This step sets up the next move, where the suggestion will be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the Torah's set price for a consecrated field is based on a בית כור. On this idea, a piece smaller than that cannot become a consecrated field. The phrase וכי תימא signals that the גמרא is about to reject this suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you will say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
an area large enough to plant a כור of seed

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. וכי תימא brings up an idea only so that it can be rejected in the next step.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
since it is not a בית כור,
they are not consecrated;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָוֵי בֵּית כּוֹר, לָא קָדְשִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense of the משנה against the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested answer (one that will be rejected)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The crevices should be consecrated as separate pieces.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pieces smaller than a בית כור cannot be consecrated, so the crevices drop out completely.

steps.title: A ברייתא: why does the פסוק say "field"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to quote a ברייתא. The ברייתא notes that the פסוק about pricing seems to speak only of a field the size of a חומר of seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: "Field": why does the פסוק say it? Because it says: "a חומר of barley seed for fifty silver shekels," I would only know about someone who consecrated this kind of field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the suggested answer by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first lays out its problem: the pricing פסוק mentions only a field the size of a חומר of seed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "field" seems unnecessary, so the ברייתא will use it to teach something. Without it, we would think the fixed price applies only to a field the size of a חומר, which is the same as a בית כור. That would actually fit the suggested answer, but the ברייתא is about to show otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a source that challenges)
why does the פסוק need to say this?
a large dry measure, the same as a כור

phrases.english: But it was taught:
"Field": why does the פסוק say it?
Because it says:
"a חומר of barley seed for fifty silver shekels";

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ בָּעִנְיָן הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: I would only know about someone who consecrated in this way,
phrases.notes: "This way" means a field big enough to plant a full חומר of seed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the source that will reject the suggested answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that a piece smaller than a בית כור cannot be consecrated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reads the extra word "field" as including smaller plots. The full point comes in step 5.

steps.title: Even tiny fields can be consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the word "field" includes much smaller plots, so any size field can be consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we include a לתך, half a לתך, a סאה, a תרקב, and half a תרקב? The פסוק says "field": in any case!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes. The word "field" teaches that even very small plots can be consecrated and priced by the Torah's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This directly rejects the suggestion from step 3 that a piece smaller than a בית כור cannot be consecrated. So the question from step 2 comes back: why aren't the deep crevices and tall rocks consecrated on their own?

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we learn to include
in any case, whatever the size

steps.whatToRemember: According to the ברייתא, a field of any size can be consecrated. So "it's smaller than a בית כור" cannot explain why the deep crevices and tall rocks are left out, and the question still stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since this answer fails, the גמרא will have to find another reason why these areas are not consecrated separately.

phrases.english: From where do we include a לתך and half a לתך,
phrases.notes: Each of these is a smaller field, named for how much seed it takes to plant it.

phrases.english: a סאה, a תרקב, and half a תרקב?
The פסוק says: "field,"
in any case!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 4 and uses it to reject step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Rejecting the claim that a piece smaller than a בית כור cannot be consecrated
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the word "field" in ויקרא 27:19 as including tiny plots

steps.title: The crevices are full of water and cannot be planted
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא answers that the teaching about הקדש is talking about crevices filled with water, which are not fit for planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא said: Here we are dealing with crevices full of water, which cannot be planted.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier answer (too small to consecrate) was knocked down, so רב עוקבא בר חמא gives a new answer. These crevices are not consecrated because they are full of water and cannot be planted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why deep crevices are not consecrated as separate plots. The new answer: consecrated fields are priced by the seed they need, so land that cannot be planted does not count. Water-filled crevices cannot be planted, so they are not consecrated at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Crevices or hollows in the ground

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama said:
Here we are dealing with crevices filled with water,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the teaching about consecrating a field from step 1.

phrases.english: which are not fit for sowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא הָכָא בִּנְקָעִים מְלֵאִים מַיִם עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from step 3, which steps 4-5 disproved.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The deep crevices are ordinary land that should be consecrated on its own.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are full of water and cannot be planted, so they cannot be consecrated at all.

steps.title: The wording 'like rocks' supports this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the teaching puts crevices together with rocks, and rocks cannot be planted. This supports רב עוקבא בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording also shows this, since it teaches crevices together with rocks. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב עוקבא בר חמא from the wording of the teaching itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching lists crevices right alongside rocks. Rocks can never be planted, so the crevices being discussed are probably ones that cannot be planted either, such as water-filled ones.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
since it teaches them like rocks;
learn from it.

steps.raayaObject: רב עוקבא בר חמא's claim that the crevices cannot be planted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching groups crevices together with rocks, which cannot be planted.

steps.title: Then small crevices should be left out too
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is that they cannot be planted, then even crevices less than ten טפחים deep should be left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even less than this should also be left out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If the reason is 'cannot be planted,' depth should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching said only crevices of ten טפחים or more are separate. Smaller ones are counted with the field. But a small water-filled crevice cannot be planted either, so why is it treated differently?

keyTerms.meaning: Less than this (less than ten טפחים)

phrases.english: If so,
even less than this as well!
phrases.notes: He means crevices less than ten טפחים deep should also not be consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן נָמֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'cannot be planted' reason of רב עוקבא בר חמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being unplantable is the reason, small unplantable crevices should also be excluded, yet the teaching counts them with the field.

steps.title: Small ones are just normal cracks and ridges
steps.stepSummary: Crevices and rocks smaller than ten טפחים are called the 'cracks of the earth' and the 'spines of the earth.' They are a normal part of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those are called 'cracks of the earth' and 'spines of the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that small crevices and rocks are seen as ordinary features of any field, not as separate spots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small hollow or bump is just part of what a field looks like, so it goes along with the field. Only a deep crevice or tall rock counts as its own area, and then its unplantable nature keeps it out.

phrases.english: those are called "cracks of the earth";
phrases.notes: This name is for the small crevices.

phrases.english: they are called "spines of the earth."
phrases.notes: This name is for the small rocks, like a backbone sticking up in the ground.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every unplantable crevice should be excluded, whatever its size.
steps.terutzMaskana: Small crevices and rocks are normal parts of the field and go along with it. Only large ones stand apart.
steps.whatToRemember: For הקדש: deep (ten טפחים) water-filled crevices and tall rocks are left out because they cannot be planted. Smaller ones are ordinary 'cracks' and 'spines' of the field and are included.

steps.title: What about crevices in a sale?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the rule is in our case of selling a field. Do deep crevices have to be full of water to be left out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from הקדש to our own case of selling a field. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הקדש the crevices had to be unplantable (full of water). Now the גמרא asks whether a sale works the same way or has a different reason.

phrases.english: Here, what?
phrases.notes: "Here" means our case of selling a field, where deep crevices are not measured with the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the הקדש discussion to the sale case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, in a sale, deep crevices are left out only if full of water.

steps.title: In a sale, even dry deep crevices are left out
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that in a sale, deep crevices are left out even without water, because a buyer does not want a field that looks split into several pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even if they are not full of water. Why? A person does not want to pay for one place and have it look like two or three places.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that in a sale the water does not matter. He gives the reason: what the buyer wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling uses a different measure than הקדש. In a sale, what counts is what the buyer expects to get. A deep crevice makes the field look broken into separate plots, which a buyer does not want, so it is not measured as part of the field even if it can be planted.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מְלֵאִים מַיִם.
phrases.english: Even if they are not filled with water.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם רוֹצֶה שֶׁיִּתֵּן מְעוֹתָיו בִּמְקוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: A person does not want to give his money for one place,
and have it look to him like two or three places.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב פָּפָּא אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מְלֵאִים מַיִם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a sale, deep crevices are excluded even when dry, because a buyer does not want a field that looks split up.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two reasons. For הקדש the reason is that the land cannot be planted. For a sale the reason is how the field looks to a buyer, so water does not matter.

steps.title: רבינא: The teaching compares crevices to rocks
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב פפא: the teaching puts crevices together with rocks, so like rocks, they must be unplantable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: But it teaches them like rocks. Just as rocks cannot be planted, these too cannot be planted!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב פפא using the same 'like rocks' wording that supported רב עוקבא בר חמא in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If crevices are compared to rocks, the shared feature seems to be that both cannot be planted. That would mean dry, plantable crevices should be measured with the field, which goes against רב פפא.

phrases.english: Ravina objected to it:
But it teaches them like rocks –

phrases.aramaic: מָה סְלָעִים דְּלָאו בְּנֵי זְרִיעָה נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: just as rocks are not fit for sowing,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הָנֵי נָמֵי דְּלָאו בְּנֵי זְרִיעָה נִינְהוּ!
phrases.english: so too these are not fit for sowing!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא וְהָא דּוּמְיָא דִּסְלָעִים קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that dry deep crevices are excluded in a sale
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison to rocks suggests only unplantable crevices are excluded, so dry crevices should be included.

steps.title: The comparison to rocks is about the small ones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the comparison to rocks is about crevices less than ten טפחים deep, not about the deep ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it teaches them like rocks, that is about the ones less than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by saying which part of the teaching the comparison to rocks belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to rocks teaches that small crevices, like small rocks, are counted with the field even though they cannot be planted. It does not say that deep crevices must be unplantable to be left out. So רב פפא's rule stands.

phrases.english: When it teaches them like rocks –
it is about less than this.
phrases.notes: Meaning crevices less than ten טפחים deep, which are measured with the field even if they can't be planted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי דּוּמְיָא דִּסְלָעִים אַפָּחוֹת מִכָּאן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning which case the wording refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to rocks means deep crevices are excluded only when unplantable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison to rocks is about small crevices being included like small rocks. Deep crevices in a sale are excluded even when dry.
steps.whatToRemember: In a sale, crevices ten טפחים deep are not measured with the field even without water, because the field looks broken up. The 'like rocks' comparison is about the small ones, which are included.

steps.title: Small rocks count with the field, up to a limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line that rocks under ten טפחים are measured with the field. רבי יצחק says this only applies up to a total area of a בית ארבעת קבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rocks or crevices smaller than ten טפחים are measured together with the field. רבי יצחק said: the rocks the Sages meant here are up to an area of four קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the teaching, that small rocks count as part of the field. Then רבי יצחק puts a limit on how much rocky ground can be counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small rocks are normally part of a field, so the buyer pays for that area too. But רבי יצחק says there is a ceiling: in a field sold as a בית כור, only up to a בית ארבעת קבין of such rocks is counted. More than that, and the buyer does not have to accept it as field.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than this (less than ten טפחים)
Are measured together with it (the field)
An area large enough to plant four קבין of seed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the deep crevices from before. Here we are talking only about the small ones (under ten טפחים), which do count as field, but only up to a limit.

phrases.english: Less than this
phrases.notes: He means less than ten טפחים, the size that was discussed in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: they are measured with it.
Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
The rocks that they spoke of
are an area of four kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן נִמְדָּדִין עִמָּהּ. אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the deep crevices to the next line, about small rocks that are counted with the field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small rocks are counted with the field only up to a total of a בית ארבעת קבין.

steps.title: The rocks must be spread over five קבין
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא adds that the four קבין of rocks count only if they are scattered within an area of five קבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא said: this is only when the rocks are spread out within an area of five קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוקבא בר חמא adds a condition to רבי יצחק's rule. It is not enough to have only four קבין of rocks; they also have to be spread out a certain way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If four קבין of rocks sit together in one solid block, it looks like a separate rocky piece, not part of the field. So רב עוקבא בר חמא says they must be scattered in among planting land, across an area of five קבין.

keyTerms.meaning: This is only when... (adds a condition)

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama said:
This is only when they are scattered
phrases.notes: Literally "swallowed up," meaning the rocks are mixed in among good land.

phrases.english: within five kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: וְהוּא שֶׁמּוּבְלָעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to רבי יצחק's limit of four קבין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rocks count with the field only if they are scattered within an area of five קבין.

steps.title: The rocks must be spread over most of the field
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a different condition: the rocks must be scattered across the majority of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this is only when the rocks are spread out across most of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: A second condition is offered, this time from רבי יוחנן. He says the rocks must be spread over most of the field, not just over five קבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions want the rocks spread out so they feel like part of the field. רבי יוחנן asks for much more spreading than רב עוקבא בר חמא: across the majority of the whole field.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Abba
said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is only when they are scattered
throughout the majority of the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְהוּא שֶׁמּוּבְלָעִין בְּרוּבָּהּ שֶׁל שָׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of the condition from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rocks count with the field only if they are scattered across most of the field.

steps.title: What if the rocks are spread unevenly?
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבא asks about a mixed case: most of the rocks sit in a small part of the field, and a few rocks are spread over the larger part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבא asked: if most of the rocks are in the smaller part of the field, and the fewer rocks are in the larger part, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבא asks a question about רבי יוחנן's rule. What happens when the rocks are spread unevenly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the rocks must be spread across most of the field. Here, the rocks do reach most of the field, but only a few of them; the bulk of the rocks are bunched in a small area. It is unclear if that counts as "spread across most of the field."

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question he could not settle)
Most of them (the rocks) in the smaller part of it (the field)
The fewer of them in the larger part of it

phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Abba asked:
Most of them in the smaller part of it,
phrases.notes: "Them" is the rocks, and "it" is the field.

phrases.english: and the fewer of them in the larger part of it,
what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the edges of רבי יוחנן's condition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an uneven spread, where only a few rocks reach most of the field, meet רבי יוחנן's condition?

steps.title: The question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the question with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot answer רב חייא בר אבא's question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the question has no clear answer from the sources. The mixed case stays unsettled.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: Small rocks count with a field up to four קבין, and they must be spread out (over five קבין, or over most of the field per רבי יוחנן). The uneven case is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 17 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of most rocks in a small area and a few rocks across most of the field stays unresolved.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה starts a new question
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה begins asking a new question; the question itself comes next.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבי ירמיה is about to ask a new question, and its content follows right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words are here. The actual question has not been said yet, so wait for the next lines to see what he asks.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the open question ends, a new question begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated; the question continues in the next lines.
